dataset.description: The adversarial teach-back set of RECON-W41. Every item offers a keyed correct answer and alternatives bound to named misconceptions, and the wrong alternatives are chosen so that their words overlap the lesson. A learner that matches on vocabulary rather than on structure is therefore fooled, and the set can tell the two measurements apart. The phases are DISJOINT: pre, post, delayed and transfer. The delayed phase is a LOGICAL delay supplied by the harness, never a wall-clock one; it validates the measurement machinery and the shape of the score, not human retention.

items.prompt: What gas does a plant release during photosynthesis, and where does it come from?

alternatives.text: Oxygen, released as the waste product of the carbon dioxide the plant absorbs.
Oxygen, released when the plant splits water.
Carbon dioxide, released when the plant breaks down sugars.

items.prompt: How do plants and animals relate to one another in the energy cycle?

alternatives.text: Plants photosynthesize and animals respire; neither needs the other.
Plants photosynthesize to store energy and animals respire to release it.
Plants and animals both photosynthesize when they are in light.

items.prompt: Why is the efficiency of photosynthesis lowered in C3 plants?

alternatives.text: Because RuBisCO binds carbon dioxide and oxygen at the same time, and the oxygenation route wastes energy.
Because RuBisCO is too slow to work in warm weather.
Because RuBisCO cannot split water under light.

items.prompt: Name the gas a green plant gives out during the light reactions, and name the molecule it comes from.

alternatives.text: Oxygen, and it comes from the water the plant takes up.
Oxygen, and it comes from the carbon dioxide the plant takes in.
Carbon dioxide, and it comes from the sugars the plant breaks down.

items.prompt: What does a photosynthetic organism need cellular respiration for?

alternatives.text: It needs respiration because photosynthesis gives it no usable energy at all.
It needs respiration to release the energy stored in sugars that photosynthesis made.
It needs respiration to make sugars from carbon dioxide.

items.prompt: A plant is supplied with carbon dioxide but the enzyme keeps binding oxygen. What is the consequence?

alternatives.text: The plant gains nothing, because the carbon dioxide cannot be fixed without RuBisCO.
The plant loses energy, because the oxygenation route leads into the wasteful photorespiratory pathway.
The plant respires faster, so it needs less light.

items.prompt: In which step of the Calvin-Benson cycle is carbon dioxide added to the molecule RuBisCO competes for?

alternatives.text: In the carboxylation step, where carbon dioxide is added to RuBP.
In the regeneration step, where RuBP is rebuilt from sugar.
In the reduction step, where the sugar is made from the acid.

items.prompt: Which molecule is broken apart to give a plant its released oxygen?

alternatives.text: The carbon dioxide, so the oxygen comes with the carbon.
The water, so the oxygen comes from the water the roots took up.
The glucose, so the oxygen comes from the sugar.

items.prompt: Explain why a photosynthetic organism still needs to respire even though it makes its own food.

alternatives.text: Because photosynthesis only works in light and respiration works in the dark.
Because the sugars it makes hold energy that respiration releases for use.
Because plants cannot use the sugars they make.

items.prompt: What happens to a leaf's stomatal conductance when the supply of carbon dioxide or water changes?

alternatives.text: It is affected by light, carbon dioxide and water supply.
It is fixed by the plant's species and cannot change.
It changes only with the temperature of the air.

items.prompt: An aquatic plant makes sugar in bright light but cannot use the carbon dioxide in the water around it. Which part of the process has failed?

alternatives.text: The carbon dioxide has not reached the site where it is fixed.
The light has not reached the leaves.
The water has not reached the roots.

items.prompt: A plant is given plenty of light and carbon dioxide but its sugars stop being made. Which enzyme has most likely stopped working?

alternatives.text: RuBisCO, the enzyme that fixes carbon dioxide.
An enzyme that splits water in the light reactions.
An enzyme that rebuilds RuBP from sugar.

items.prompt: A C4 plant and a cyanobacterium both raise the carbon dioxide around RuBisCO. What do they have in common?

alternatives.text: Both concentrate carbon dioxide so that RuBisCO fixes more of it.
Both release oxygen in the light reactions of the thylakoid membrane.
Both respire at night to store sugar.
